newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index hits record in active week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index hits record in active week.

text.p: Kuwait share index rose 43.8 points to a 2,216.9 peak during the week to Thursday with expected privatisations fueling an active trade, dealers said.
"There has been talk about coming privatisations. That is expected to keep the demand in high levels next week," said a portfolio manager.

State selloffs of stakes in listed firms, under a three-year- old privatisation programme, traditionally boost demand on selective shares. The market is expecting official privatisation announcements in the near future, dealers said.
"Good performance by listed firms in the first quarter seem to be encouraging also," said Hassan, a privat dealer.
Gainers led losers 25-18 while 17 were non-movers, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
The daily average for value of traded shares edged up to 56.2 million dinars ($185.5 million) from 54 million. Volume clocked up to a daily average of 213 million shares from 188.6 million.
Property firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 118 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 91.2 million and banks with 45.2 million.
Kuwait Real Estate, United Realty, National Real Estate, Investment Projects, The International Investor and Commercial Bank were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
